ei.title: Munjado, a Window into the Joseon Dynasty
ei.subject: 중3

fullPassage:
Look at the painting on the right. Do you see the Chinese character, hyo (孝)? Do you also see a carp, a geomungo, and a fan? This kind of painting is called Munjado, and it is a type of folk painting that was popular in the late Joseon dynasty. In Munjado, there is usually a Chinese character with some animals or objects. One of eight Chinese characters appears in Munjado. They are hyo (孝), je (悌), chung (忠), sin (信), ye (禮), ui (義), yeom (廉), and chi (恥), and they represent the values that were important to people of the Joseon dynasty.

The animals or objects in Munjado are not just decorations. They often are symbolic. For example, carp in the paintings of hyo symbolize respect for parents because of an old story. The story goes as follows. Once upon a time, a man lived with his old mother. One winter, the man's mother became ill and couldn't eat anything. On one very cold day, the mother said to the man, "It would be wonderful if I could eat fresh fish." The man went out to the river, but it was completely frozen. It was impossible for him to catch any fish. The man was so disappointed that he cried out to the sky, "What should I do? Please help me." Then the ice melted, and three carp suddenly came out of the water. The man went back home and cooked the fish for his mother. Then his mother got well.

There are other examples of symbolic objects in Munjado. They are bamboo in the paintings of the character chung (忠) and lotus flowers in the paintings of ui (義). Bamboo does not bend. It stays green in all kinds of weather. For these reasons, bamboo came to symbolize loyalty to the king. In the case of lotus flowers, they grow in muddy ponds but still bloom beautifully. They thus became a symbol of a person's will to fight for justice despite difficulties. Munjado was much more than a painting to people of the Joseon dynasty. It reminded them of important values that greatly influenced their behaviors and attitudes. In particular, for children, Munjado was a study tool. Through it, children in the Joseon dynasty could learn the importance of harmony in family and society.

det.korean: 'One of eight Chinese characters'의 진짜 주어는 One(단수)이므로 동사는 appears가 맞다. appear는 틀림.

❌ ④ represent : 주어 they(복수)에 맞는 동사원형, 맞음.
det.tip: One of the + 복수명사 → 동사는 단수(appears).

det.korean: 문자도의 사물은 상징적이고(symbolic), 잉어는 공경(respect)을 상징한다. 어머니는 병이 들어(ill) 아무것도 못 먹었고, 물고기 잡기는 불가능했다(impossible).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ well(건강한)이 부적절 — 어머니는 아무것도 먹지 못했으므로 '병이 든(ill)' 상태여야 한다.
❌ ① symbolic(상징적인) : 사물이 상징적이다로 적절.
❌ ② respect(공경) : 부모에 대한 공경으로 적절.
❌ ④ impossible(불가능한) : 물고기 잡기가 불가능함으로 적절.
det.tip: ill = 아픈 ↔ well = 건강한(문맥에 반대).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 대나무는 구부러지지(bend) 않고 푸르러서(green) 충성심(loyalty)을 상징하며, 아이들은 가족·사회의 조화(harmony)의 중요성을 배웠다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ conflict(갈등)가 부적절 — 아이들은 가족·사회의 '조화(harmony)'의 중요성을 배웠다고 해야 맞다.
❌ ① bend(구부러지다) : 대나무가 구부러지지 않음으로 적절.
❌ ② green(푸른) : 어떤 날씨에도 푸름으로 적절.
❌ ③ loyalty(충성심) : 왕에 대한 충성심으로 적절.
det.tip: harmony = 조화 ↔ conflict = 갈등.

questions.passage: Once upon a time, a man lived with his old mother. One winter, the man's mother became ill and couldn't eat anything. On one very cold day, the mother said to the man, "It would be wonderful if I could eat fresh fish." The man went out to the river, but it was completely frozen. It was impossible for him to catch any fish. The man was so disappointed that he cried out to the sky, "What should I do? Please help me." Then the ice melted, and three carp suddenly came out of the water. The man went back home and cooked the fish for his mother.

Q: What was completely frozen when the man went out in winter?

det.korean: 본문 'The man went out to the river, but it was completely frozen'에서 완전히 얼어붙은 것은 '강(river)'이다.

det.tip: the river was completely frozen = 강이 완전히 얼었다.

questions.passage: There are other examples of symbolic objects in Munjado. They are bamboo in the paintings of the character chung (忠) and lotus flowers in the paintings of ui (義). Bamboo does not bend. It stays green in all kinds of weather. For these reasons, bamboo came to symbolize loyalty to the king. In the case of lotus flowers, they grow in muddy ponds but still bloom beautifully. They thus became a symbol of a person's will to fight for justice despite difficulties. Munjado was much more than a painting to people of the Joseon dynasty. It reminded them of important values that greatly influenced their behaviors and attitudes. In particular, for children, Munjado was a study tool. Through it, children in the Joseon dynasty could learn the importance of harmony in family and society.

det.analysis: 질문의 빈칸은 연꽃이 자라는 장소이다. 본문에 'grow in muddy ponds'라고 나오므로 형용사 muddy + 명사 ponds, 즉 muddy ponds 가 정답이다.

questions.passage: Look at the painting on the right. Do you see the Chinese character, hyo (孝)? Do you also see a carp, a geomungo, and a fan? This kind of painting is called Munjado, and it is a type of folk painting that was popular in the late Joseon dynasty. In Munjado, there is usually a Chinese character with some animals or objects. One of eight Chinese characters appears in Munjado. They are hyo (孝), je (悌), chung (忠), sin (信), ye (禮), ui (義), yeom (廉), and chi (恥), and they represent the values that were important to people of the Joseon dynasty.
